_readme: Vital Stats' curated national set. Every figure was read live on the publisher's own page on the date in `checked`, and `quote` is the sentence (or table row) it came from, kept so the next check is a comparison, not a hunt. `quote` stays in this file; scripts/build-vital-stats.js drops it from the shipped bank. To refresh: open each url, compare the quote, update a / year / quote / checked together, then run node scripts/build-vital-stats.js. If a page stops stating a number plainly, delete the question rather than guess.

questions.q: How much did the U.S. spend on health care in 2024, in trillions of dollars?
questions.src: CMS, National Health Expenditure fact sheet
questions.why: Spending grew 7.2 percent that year.
questions.quote: NHE grew 7.2% to $5.3 trillion in 2024, or $15,474 per person

questions.q: How much did the U.S. spend on health care per person in 2024, in dollars?
questions.src: CMS, National Health Expenditure fact sheet
questions.why: CMS divides total national health spending by the whole U.S. population, insured or not.
questions.quote: NHE grew 7.2% to $5.3 trillion in 2024, or $15,474 per person

questions.q: What share of U.S. gross domestic product went to health care in 2024, as a percent?
questions.src: CMS, National Health Expenditure fact sheet
questions.why: The figure comes from the National Health Expenditure Accounts, which CMS keeps back to 1960.
questions.quote: and accounted for 18.0% of Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

questions.q: How much did the U.S. spend on hospital care in 2024, in billions of dollars?
questions.src: CMS, National Health Expenditure fact sheet
questions.why: Hospital spending grew 8.9 percent in 2024, faster than health spending as a whole.
questions.quote: Hospital expenditures grew 8.9% to $1,634.7 billion in 2024

questions.q: How much did the U.S. spend on retail prescription drugs in 2024, in billions of dollars?
questions.src: CMS, National Health Expenditure 2024 highlights
questions.why: Retail drug spending grew 7.9 percent; drugs given in hospitals and clinics are counted with those settings instead.
questions.quote: Retail prescription drug spending increased 7.9 percent to $467.0 billion in 2024

questions.q: How much did people in the U.S. pay out of pocket for health care in 2024, in billions of dollars?
questions.src: CMS, National Health Expenditure fact sheet
questions.why: Out-of-pocket spending was 11 percent of the national total.
questions.quote: Out of pocket spending grew 5.9% to $556.6 billion in 2024, or 11 percent of total NHE.

questions.q: What was the average annual premium for employer-sponsored family health coverage in 2025, in dollars?
questions.src: KFF, 2025 Employer Health Benefits Survey
questions.why: Single coverage averaged $9,325 the same year.
questions.quote: The average annual premiums for employer-sponsored health insurance in 2025 are $9,325 for single coverage and $26,993 for family coverage.

questions.q: On average, how much did workers contribute toward employer family coverage in 2025, in dollars per year?
questions.src: KFF, 2025 Employer Health Benefits Survey
questions.why: That is the worker's share of the premium alone, before any deductible or copay.
questions.quote: On average, workers contributed $6,850 toward the cost of family coverage.

questions.q: In 2025, what was the average annual deductible for single coverage among covered workers whose plan has one, in dollars?
questions.src: KFF, 2025 Employer Health Benefits Survey
questions.why: The average leaves out workers whose plan has no general annual deductible.
questions.quote: The average deductible among covered workers in a plan with a general annual deductible was $1,886 for single coverage.

questions.q: In 2022, employers and private insurers paid hospitals what percent of what Medicare would have paid for the same care?
questions.src: RAND, hospital price study, round 5.1
questions.why: RAND's next round, on 2023 to 2025 claims, is expected in September 2027.
questions.quote: In 2022, ... employers and private insurers paid, on average, 254 percent of what Medicare would have paid

questions.q: What is the standard monthly Medicare Part B premium in 2026, in dollars?
questions.src: CMS, 2026 Medicare Parts A and B premiums and deductibles fact sheet
questions.why: The Part B annual deductible for 2026 is $283.
questions.quote: The standard monthly premium for Medicare Part B enrollees will be $202.90 for 2026

questions.q: What is the Medicare Part A inpatient hospital deductible in 2026, in dollars?
questions.src: CMS, 2026 Medicare Parts A and B premiums and deductibles fact sheet
questions.why: It applies to each benefit period, so a second admission months later can trigger it again.
questions.quote: The Medicare Part A inpatient hospital deductible that beneficiaries pay if admitted to the hospital will be $1,736 in 2026

questions.q: What percent of people in the U.S. were uninsured for all of 2025?
questions.src: U.S. Census Bureau, Health Insurance Coverage in the United States: 2025
questions.why: The Census Bureau found it was not statistically different from 2024.
questions.quote: In 2025, 26.7 million people (7.9 percent) were uninsured for the entire year, not statistically different from 2024.

questions.q: How many people in the U.S. were uninsured for all of 2025, in millions?
questions.src: U.S. Census Bureau, Health Insurance Coverage in the United States: 2025
questions.why: The count only includes people who had no coverage at any point in the year.
questions.quote: In 2025, 26.7 million people (7.9 percent) were uninsured for the entire year, not statistically different from 2024.

questions.q: What percent of people in the U.S. had employment-based health insurance for some or all of 2025?
questions.src: U.S. Census Bureau, Health Insurance Coverage in the United States: 2025
questions.why: It was the most common type of coverage, ahead of Medicare at 20.1 percent and Medicaid at 17.1 percent.
questions.quote: Employment-based insurance was the most common, covering 53.5 percent of the population for some or all of the calendar year, followed by Medicare (20.1 percent), Medicaid (17.1 percent).

questions.q: How many people were enrolled in Medicare in June 2026, in millions?
questions.src: CMS, Medicare Monthly Enrollment (national total, June 2026)
questions.why: The total counts people in Original Medicare and in Medicare Advantage.
questions.quote: YEAR 2026, MONTH June, BENE_GEO_LVL National, TOT_BENES 70609057

questions.q: What percent of eligible Medicare beneficiaries are enrolled in Medicare Advantage in 2026?
questions.src: KFF, Medicare Advantage in 2026: Enrollment Update and Key Trends
questions.why: That is 35.2 million of the 64.2 million people eligible.
questions.quote: More than half (55%) of eligible Medicare beneficiaries are enrolled in Medicare Advantage in 2026

questions.q: How many people were enrolled in Medicaid and CHIP in May 2026, in millions?
questions.src: CMS, Medicaid and CHIP Enrollment Data, report highlights
questions.why: Medicaid alone accounted for 66.4 million of them.
questions.quote: 73,526,272 people were enrolled in Medicaid and CHIP in the 50 states and the District of Columbia that reported enrollment data for May 2026.

questions.q: How many people selected an ACA Marketplace plan in the 2026 open enrollment period, in millions?
questions.src: CMS, 2026 Open Enrollment Report
questions.why: About 15.8 million came through HealthCare.gov and 7.4 million through state-based exchanges.
questions.quote: During the 2026 OEP, 23.1 million consumers selected or were automatically re-enrolled in health insurance coverage

questions.q: As of 2026, how many states, counting DC, have adopted the ACA Medicaid expansion?
questions.src: KFF, Status of State Medicaid Expansion Decisions
questions.why: Ten states have not adopted it.
questions.quote: To date, 41 states (including DC) have adopted the Medicaid expansion and 10 states have not adopted the expansion.

questions.q: How much did Medicare spend in 2024, in billions of dollars?
questions.src: CMS, National Health Expenditure fact sheet
questions.why: Medicare was 21 percent of all U.S. health spending that year.
questions.quote: Medicare spending grew 7.8% to $1,118.0 billion in 2024, or 21 percent of total NHE.

questions.q: How many registered nurses were employed in the U.S. in May 2025?
questions.src: BLS, Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2025, Table 1
questions.why: The mean annual wage for the group was $101,420.

questions.q: How many respiratory therapists were employed in the U.S. in May 2025?
questions.src: BLS, Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2025, Table 1
questions.why: BLS put their mean hourly wage at $41.97.
questions.quote: Respiratory therapists | 139,790 | $41.97 | $87,300 | $39.56

questions.q: How many nurse practitioners were employed in the U.S. in May 2025?
questions.src: BLS, Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2025, Table 1
questions.why: Physician assistants, the neighboring role, numbered 162,150.

questions.q: How many home health and personal care aides were employed in the U.S. in May 2025?
questions.src: BLS, Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2025, Table 1
questions.why: The median hourly wage for the job was $17.21.
questions.quote: Home health and personal care aides | 4,305,810 | $17.36 | $36,120 | $17.21

questions.q: How many active physicians were there in the U.S. in 2024?
questions.src: AAMC, 2025 Physician Specialty Data key findings
questions.why: Of those, 866,460 were in direct patient care.
questions.quote: In 2024, the United States had 1,032,365 active physicians of which 866,460 were direct patient care physicians

questions.q: AAMC projects a U.S. physician shortage of up to how many physicians by 2036?
questions.src: AAMC, physician workforce projections (March 2024)
questions.why: The projection came out in March 2024 and is still AAMC's latest.
questions.quote: the United States will face a physician shortage of up to 86,000 physicians by 2036.

questions.q: What was the median age of registered nurses in the U.S. in 2024, in years?
questions.src: NCSBN, 2024 National Nursing Workforce Survey
questions.why: The median was 46 in the 2022 survey.
questions.quote: The median age of RNs was 50 in 2024, increasing from a median age of 46 in 2022

questions.q: How many people worked in the U.S. health care industry in August 2026, in millions?
questions.src: BLS, Current Employment Statistics, Table B-1 (preliminary, seasonally adjusted)
questions.why: Ambulatory care was the biggest piece at about 9.2 million jobs, ahead of hospitals at 5.8 million.
questions.quote: Health care | ... | 18,520.7 (thousands; ambulatory 9,248.5, hospitals 5,776.5, nursing and residential care 3,495.7)

questions.q: As of 2026, how many jurisdictions are part of the Nurse Licensure Compact?
questions.src: NCSBN, Nurse Licensure Compact
questions.why: The compact lets one multistate license cover practice in the member jurisdictions.
questions.quote: 43 jurisdictions are currently part of the NLC.

questions.q: How many hospitals were there in the U.S. in 2024, per the AHA Annual Survey?
questions.src: AHA, Fast Facts on U.S. Hospitals, 2026 edition (2024 Annual Survey)
questions.why: The total includes federal and psychiatric hospitals, not only community hospitals.
questions.quote: There are 6,100 hospitals in the United States.

questions.q: How many community hospitals were there in the U.S. in 2024?
questions.src: AHA, Fast Facts on U.S. Hospitals, 2026 edition (2024 Annual Survey)
questions.why: AHA counts nonfederal, short-term general and specialty hospitals open to the public as community hospitals.
questions.quote: Number of U.S. Community Hospitals 5,121

questions.q: How many rural community hospitals were there in the U.S. in 2024?
questions.src: AHA, Fast Facts on U.S. Hospitals, 2026 edition (2024 Annual Survey)
questions.why: That is about a third of the country's 5,121 community hospitals.
questions.quote: Number of Rural Community Hospitals 1,797

questions.q: How many staffed beds were there across all U.S. hospitals in 2024?
questions.src: AHA, Fast Facts on U.S. Hospitals, 2026 edition (2024 Annual Survey)
questions.why: Staffed beds are the ones set up and staffed for patients, which can be fewer than the licensed count.
questions.quote: Total Staffed Beds in All U.S. Hospitals 907,216

questions.q: How many admissions did all U.S. hospitals record in 2024, in millions?
questions.src: AHA, Fast Facts on U.S. Hospitals, 2026 edition (2024 Annual Survey)
questions.why: AHA's exact count was 35,658,583.
questions.quote: Total Admissions in All U.S. Hospitals 35,658,583

questions.q: What was life expectancy at birth for the U.S. population in 2024, in years?
questions.src: CDC NCHS, Mortality in the United States, 2024 (Data Brief 548)
questions.why: That was up 0.6 year from 2023.
questions.quote: Life expectancy for the U.S. population was 79.0 years in 2024, an increase of 0.6 year from 2023.

questions.q: How many people in the U.S. died of heart disease in 2024?
questions.src: CDC NCHS, Mortality in the United States, 2024 (Data Brief 548)
questions.why: Heart disease was the leading cause of death that year.
questions.quote: Diseases of heart ... 683,491 ... 157.6

questions.q: How many drug overdose deaths occurred in the U.S. in 2024?
questions.src: CDC NCHS, Drug Overdose Deaths in the United States, 2023 to 2024 (Data Brief 549)
questions.why: The age-adjusted rate fell from 31.3 per 100,000 in 2023 to 23.1 in 2024.
questions.quote: In 2024, 79,384 drug overdose deaths occurred, resulting in an age-adjusted rate of 23.1 deaths per 100,000 standard population

questions.q: How many suicide deaths were recorded in the U.S. in 2024?
questions.src: CDC NCHS, Mortality in the United States, 2024 (Data Brief 548)
questions.why: Suicide was the 10th leading cause of death in 2024.
questions.quote: Intentional self-harm (suicide) ... 48,824 ... 13.7

questions.q: What was the U.S. infant mortality rate in 2024, in infant deaths per 100,000 live births?
questions.src: CDC NCHS, Mortality in the United States, 2024 (Data Brief 548)
questions.why: That is about 5.5 per 1,000, the way the rate is usually quoted.
questions.quote: The infant mortality rate in 2024 (552.5 infant deaths per 100,000 live births) was not significantly different from the 2023 rate (560.2).

questions.q: What was the U.S. maternal mortality rate in 2024, in deaths per 100,000 live births?
questions.src: CDC NCHS, Maternal Mortality Rates in the United States, 2024 (Health E-Stat 113)
questions.why: 649 women died of maternal causes that year.
questions.quote: In 2024, 649 women died of maternal causes... The maternal mortality rate for 2024, 17.9 deaths per 100,000 live births

questions.q: How many babies were born in the U.S. in 2025, in millions?
questions.src: CDC NCHS, Births: Provisional Data for 2025 (VSRR 43)
questions.why: The provisional count of 3,606,400 was down 1 percent from 2024.
questions.quote: The provisional number of births for the United States in 2025 was 3,606,400, a 1% decline from 2024.

questions.q: How many people in the U.S. had diabetes in 2023, diagnosed or not, in millions?
questions.src: CDC, National Diabetes Statistics Report
questions.why: That is 12.0 percent of the U.S. population.
questions.quote: 40.1 million Estimated number of people with diagnosed or undiagnosed diabetes in the United States, 2023

questions.q: What percent of U.S. adults had obesity from August 2021 to August 2023?
questions.src: CDC NCHS, Obesity and Severe Obesity Prevalence in Adults (Data Brief 508, NHANES)
questions.why: NHANES measures height and weight in person instead of asking people to report them.
questions.quote: During August 2021–August 2023, the prevalence of obesity in adults was 40.3%

questions.q: What percent of U.S. adults currently smoked cigarettes in 2025?
questions.src: CDC NCHS, FastStats: Smoking (National Health Interview Survey, 2025 early release)
questions.why: The survey's confidence interval runs from 8.6 to 9.7 percent.
questions.quote: Percent of adults age 18 and older who currently smoke cigarettes: 9.1%
